author: beehive state news
title: Utah baseball loses to Kansas State in Big 12 Tournament opener
text:
The Utah baseball team lost to Kansas State, 9-5, on May 20 in the opening round of the Big 12 Tournament at Surprise Stadium.
The game was tied at five runs each after seven innings before Kansas State scored four runs in the eighth inning to secure the win. Utah’s Luke Jacobs and Jake Long each went 3-for-5 at the plate. Jacobs hit a solo home run and scored twice, while Long doubled twice, drove in two runs, and also scored two times.
Matt Flaharty extended his hitting streak to eleven games, marking his longest career streak. Jake Long recorded his team-leading twenty-fourth multi-hit game of the season. Demitri Diamant started for Utah (26-25) and pitched three shutout innings as eight pitchers took turns on the mound throughout the game.
Utah opened scoring with three runs in the fifth inning after Derek Smith singled and advanced on hits by Jacobs and Long. Cal Miller added another run with a single that allowed Long to score. Kansas State responded with a two-run homer in the sixth inning before taking their first lead with three more runs in the seventh.
Jacobs brought Utah back within reach with a solo home run early in their half of the seventh inning, followed by Miller’s sacrifice fly that tied it up again. However, Kansas State’s four-run rally during a lengthy eighth inning—partly due to an overturned call after video review—put them ahead for good.
As seen during their regular season matchups, Utah threatened late but could not complete a comeback against Kansas State.
